title: Eczema Area et gravité index (EASI)
formula:
Total EASI = addition of EASI for each body region (i.e., head/neck, upper limbs, trunk, and lower limbs)

EASI for each body region = severity score x area score x multiplier

The severity score is calculated by the addition of the selected points:

| Lesion characteristic | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Redness (erythema, inflammation) | None, absent | 0 |
| Mild (just perceptible) | 1 | |
| Moderate (obvious) | 2 | |
| Severe | 3 | |
| Thickness (induration, papulation, swelling; acute eczema) | None, absent | 0 |
| Mild (just perceptible) | 1 | |
| Moderate (obvious) | 2 | |
| Severe | 3 | |
| Scratching (excoriation) | None, absent | 0 |
| Mild (just perceptible) | 1 | |
| Moderate (obvious) | 2 | |
| Severe | 3 | |
| Lichenification (lined skin, furrowing, prurigo nodule; chronic eczema) | None, absent | 0 |
| Mild (just perceptible) | 1 | |
| Moderate (obvious) | 2 | |
| Severe | 3 | |

The area score is determined as follows:

| Percentage of region affected | Area Score |
| --- | --- |
| 0% (no active eczema in region) | 0 |
| 1-9% | 1 |
| 10-29% | 2 |
| 30-49% | 3 |
| 50-69% | 4 |
| 70-89% | 5 |
| 90-100% ( entire region affected by eczema) | 6 |

The multiplier is determined as follows:

| Region affected | Constants |
| --- | --- |
| Head/neck | 0.1 |
| Upper limbs | 0.2 |
| Trunk | 0.3 |
| Lower limbs | 0.4 |

how_to_use.why:
- Easily understood and simple system used to track disease progression.
- May be used in pediatric patients.
- Used in clinical trials of therapies for atopic dermatitis.
- In Australia, EASI is used to determine eligibility for government subsidized prescription drugs.
how_to_use.when: Patients >8 years old with atopic dermatitis, to assess severity and extent.
how_to_use.pearls:
- EASI is one of the most widely used instruments in assessing atopic dermatitis in both clinical and trial settings.
- EASI is less reliable when assessing patients with darker skin.

next_steps.advice:
- The higher the EASI score, the higher the severity of atopic dermatitis.
- Recording the trend of EASI score helps with assessing the effectiveness of a treatment.
next_steps.critical_actions: Consultation with a dermatologist may be warranted in patients with atopic dermatitis.

evidence:
- The Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) was first described in 1998 by[Tofte et al](https://www.scienceopen.com/document?vid=03a4dc8d-2669-456f-94a8-a1f826f70615). In 2001,[Hanifin et al](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/11168575)presented the assessment of reliability of EASI in atopic dermatitis (AD). This assessment was performed over 2 successive days on 15 dermatologist evaluators. EASI was found to have fair-to-good overall intra-evaluator reliability and good inter-evaluator reliability. EASI was considered an easily understood and simple tool for the evaluation of AD.
- More studies were later done to further validate EASI.[Barbier et al in 2004](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/14746622)looked at the use of EASI for atopic dermatitis in a cohort of 1,550 patients in RCTs of 1% pimecrolimus cream. EASI showed good criterion and construct validity, reliability, and sensitivity to change, and correlated well with other measures of disease severity and pruritus assessment. Internal consistency was good in all components except for lichenification. EASI, however, did not correlate well with quality of life.
- In 2007, a systematic review on outcome measures of AD by[Schmitt et al](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17910890)found that EASI has adequate convergent and divergent construct validity, adequate sensitivity to change and adequate content validity. Based on the criteria in this study, test-retest reliability, interobserver reliability and internal consistency were considered acceptable.
- In 2013[Schmitt et al](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/24035157)performed a systematic review on measurement properties of outcome measurements for clinical signs of atopic dermatitis. EASI is valid and internally consistent and has adequate intraobserver reliability, intermediate interobserver reliability and adequate responsiveness. Despite this, EASI has its drawbacks, including lack of interpretability (definition of ranges of EASI that represent mild, moderate and severe) and the absence of floor or ceiling effect.
- To improve interpretability of EASI,[Lesham et al](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25580670)suggested severity strata, later revised by[Chopra et al](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/28485036)in 2017: 0 = clear; 1-5.9 = mild; 6-22.9 = moderate; 23-72 = severe.
- One of the pitfalls in most AD severity scales (including EASI) is its reliability in patients with dark skin. In 2015,[Zhao et al](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5418878/)studied the reliability and validity of outcome measures in patients with different levels of skin pigmentation. Overall, outcome measures including EASI have poor reliability and validity in patients with dark skin. To date, there is no specific outcome measure for this cohort of patients.
more_info:
Interpretation:

A higher EASI score indicates higher severity of atopic dermatitis. Scores range from 0 (no disease) to 72 (maximal disease severity).
